svg.title: Reading request bodies: Time per call, shorter is faster
svg.text: Reading request bodies: Time per call, shorter is faster
Chat requests with an embedded image, 1 KiB to 8 MiB, and a small SSE frame; top-right: the best order-preserving competitor ÷ ojson; each panel has its own scale
Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 @ 3.20GHz · linux/amd64 · Go 1.26.6 · GOMAXPROCS=1 on one pinned CPU · median of 5 or 15 samples each
Shared KVM virtual machine with other users' load; results apply to this machine only
Other ojson rows carry their own multiplier after the value; SetBytes is compared with sjson only.
Rows that ran in rounds, one process per row and round, use the median of the per-round time ratios; bars are the medians of all samples.
Outputs were checked before timing: ojson matches gjson and sjson byte for byte, sonic/ast after compacting.
ojson and gjson use GetManyBytes for several paths and GetBytes for one; NoCopy uses GetManyBytesNoCopy and GetBytesNoCopy; sonic.Get runs once per path.
Measured with bench/json/race and bench/json/complex, drawn by bench/json/race/plot.py
Versions: tidwall/gjson v1.19.0 · tidwall/sjson v1.2.5 · bytedance/sonic v1.15.5
